answer: Tie each identity to one name on the voter roll. First, onboarding checks the applicant against the electoral registry: one voter, one agent. Second, the roll is re-checked each epoch, and a removed or duplicate name kills the identity. Third, random audits check the turnout record for a real vote in the last election. Faking 1,000 voters means 1,000 counts of fraud, each up to 5 years in prison and a 10,000 dollar fine. A raven cannot vote in a thousand precincts, and an orchard of paper voters is a mirror trick: rows of names, no real person behind any of them.
